## 1. Read the data

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(dplyr)

dataset <- read.csv("data/ess_lab.csv")

# the two variables we need
dataset |>
  select(eduyrs, lrscale) |>
  head()
```

```{r}
suppressMessages(library(dplyr))
dataset <- read.csv("../data/ess_lab.csv")
dataset |>
  select(eduyrs, lrscale) |>
  head()
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%" .fe-note}
- European Social Survey, round 11: one row per respondent, `r format(nrow(dataset), big.mark = ",")` rows
- `eduyrs`: years of education
- `lrscale`: left-right self-placement, 0 = left, 10 = right
- Both use 77, 88, 99 for missing answers
:::
::::

## 2. Clean

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
# missing codes become NA
dataset$lrscale_clean <- ifelse(
  dataset$lrscale %in% c(77, 88, 99),
  NA,
  dataset$lrscale
)

# keep 4 to 24 years (the rest becomes NA)
dataset$edu <- ifelse(
  dataset$eduyrs >= 4 & dataset$eduyrs <= 24,
  dataset$eduyrs,
  NA
)
```
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
# check
range(dataset$lrscale_clean, na.rm = TRUE)
range(dataset$edu, na.rm = TRUE)
```

::: {.fe-note}
- Always check after cleaning: 0 to 10, and 4 to 24
- Outside 4 to 24 years: `r round(100 * mean(dataset$eduyrs < 4 | (dataset$eduyrs > 24 & !dataset$eduyrs %in% c(77, 88, 99))), 1)`% of respondents. Dropping them keeps the plot readable
:::
:::
::::

## 3. Model

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
model <- lm(lrscale_clean ~ edu, data = dataset)
summary(model)
```

```{r}
model <- lm(lrscale_clean ~ edu, data = dataset)
printCoefmat(coef(summary(model)), digits = 3, signif.legend = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
# the same as a table, with 95% confidence intervals
parameters::model_parameters(model)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)

# the plot in the listing, with every part switched on or off:
# a part that is off is drawn transparent, so it still takes its space
# and every card lines up exactly with the others
card_plot <- function(on) {
  col <- function(part, colour) {
    if (part %in% on) colour else "transparent"
  }
  dataset |>
    ggplot(aes(x = edu, y = lrscale_clean)) +
    stat_summary(
      fun = mean,
      geom = "point",
      colour = col("points", "black")
    ) +
    geom_smooth(
      method = "lm",
      colour = col("line", "#3366FF"),
      fill = col("line", "grey60")
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 24, 4)) +
    labs(
      x = "Years of education",
      y = "Left-right (0 = left, 10 = right)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(
      base_size = 21,
      base_family = "Source Sans Static"
    ) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_line(colour = col("grid", "grey92")),
      axis.text.y = element_text(colour = col("y_text", "grey30")),
      axis.text.x = element_text(colour = col("x_text", "grey30")),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = col("titles", "black")),
      # transparent card: ggplot2 4 gives theme_minimal() a white background
      plot.background = element_rect(
        fill = "transparent",
        colour = NA
      )
    )
}

# check: geom_smooth(method = "lm") draws the model from step 3
smooth <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
  ggplot_build(card_plot("line"))$data[[2]]
))
smooth_slope <- diff(range(smooth$y)) / diff(range(smooth$x))

# the y axis range ggplot chooses (for the last caption)
y_axis <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
  ggplot_build(card_plot("line"))$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y.range
))
y_axis <- format(round(y_axis, 1), nsmall = 1)
stopifnot(abs(smooth_slope - abs(coef(model)[["edu"]])) < 1e-9)

# one card per block of code, in code order (bottom to top of the stack)
cards <- list(
  ggplot = "y_text",
  stat_summary = "points",
  geom_smooth = "line",
  scale_x_continuous = "x_text",
  labs = "titles",
  theme_minimal = "grid"
)

# draw each card as a transparent PNG and keep it as a data URI
card_uri <- function(on) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ragg::agg_png(
    f,
    width = 7,
    height = 5.425,
    units = "in",
    res = 170,
    background = "transparent"
  )
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(print(card_plot(on))))
  dev.off()
  knitr::image_uri(f)
}
card_images <- lapply(cards, card_uri)
```

## 4. Plot: how a ggplot is built {.ol-slide}

:::::: {.columns}
::::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(ggplot2)

dataset |>
  ggplot(aes(x = edu, y = lrscale_clean)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 24, 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Years of education",
    y = "Left-right (0 = left, 10 = right)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 21)
```

:::: {.ol-captions}
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="0"}
Each `+` adds one piece.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="1"}
Lay the plot down…
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="2"}
…and pull it apart: one card per block of code.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="3"}
`dataset |> ggplot(aes(...))`: the data and the mapping, `edu` on x and `lrscale_clean` on y. This sets up the axes.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="4"}
`stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point")`: one dot per year of education, the mean left-right position of everyone with that many years.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="5"}
`geom_smooth(method = "lm")`: the regression line from step 3 (slope `r format(b(model, "edu"), nsmall = 3)`), fitted on all respondents, not on the dots. Grey band: its 95% confidence interval.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="6"}
`scale_x_continuous()`: puts the x axis numbers at 4, 8, …, 24.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="7"}
`labs()`: the axis titles.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="8"}
`theme_minimal()`: the look. Here: no grey background, light grid lines, text size 21.
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="9"}
Stack the cards again…
:::
::: {.ol-cap data-stage="10"}
…and it is one plot. Mind the y axis: it shows only `r y_axis[1]` to `r y_axis[2]` of the 0 to 10 scale, which makes the slope look steep.
:::
::::
:::::

## 5. Make it publication ready {.pub-slide}

```{r}
#| include: false
# the step 4 plot with the first `step` changes (0 = none, 3 = all)
pub_plot <- function(step) {
  p <- dataset |>
    ggplot(aes(x = edu, y = lrscale_clean)) +
    stat_summary(
      fun = mean,
      geom = "point",
      size = if (step >= 1) 3 else 1.5,
      colour = if (step >= 1) "grey55" else "black"
    ) +
    geom_smooth(
      method = "lm",
      colour = if (step >= 2) "black" else "#3366FF"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 24, 4)) +
    labs(
      x = "Years of education",
      y = "Left-right (0 = left, 10 = right)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 21, base_family = "Source Sans Static")
  if (step >= 3) {
    p <- p +
      theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black")
      )
  }
  p
}

# one image per step, as data URIs
pub_uri <- function(step) {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ragg::agg_png(f, width = 7, height = 5.425, units = "in", res = 170)
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(print(pub_plot(step))))
  dev.off()
  knitr::image_uri(f)
}
pub_images <- lapply(0:3, pub_uri)
```

:::::: {.columns}
::::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
    size = 3,
    colour = "grey55"
  ) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "black") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(4, 24, 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Years of education",
    y = "Left-right (0 = left, 10 = right)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 21) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "black")
  )
```
:::::

::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {.pub-captions}
::: {.pub-cap data-stage="0"}
The plot from step 4. Three small changes:
:::
::: {.pub-cap data-stage="1"}
1\. Data in the background: bigger grey dots
:::
::: {.pub-cap data-stage="2"}
2\. The result in front: a black line (prints in greyscale too)
:::
::: {.pub-cap data-stage="3"}
3\. Less ink: only horizontal grid lines, and a baseline
:::
::: {.pub-cap data-stage="4"}
No title inside the figure: in a journal, it goes in the caption.
:::
::::

## Learn more

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
**Install** (once per computer)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

**Load** (every session)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(ggplot2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="60%" .ol-links}
**Free online**

- [ggplot2 website](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/): reference for every function, and [where to start learning](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/#learning-ggplot2)
- [Cheat sheet: Data visualization with ggplot2](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/data-visualization.html)
- *R for Data Science* (2e): [Data visualization](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-visualize) and [Communication](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/communication) (titles, labels, themes)
- [*R Graphics Cookbook*, 2nd edition](https://r-graphics.org/) (Winston Chang): one recipe per plot problem
- [*ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis*](https://ggplot2-book.org/) (3e): how ggplot2 works inside

**The theory**

- [*The Grammar of Graphics*](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/0-387-28695-0) (Leland Wilkinson, 2005): the idea behind ggplot2's layers (a book, not free)
:::
::::
